title: Evaluating the Impact of Fertilizer Subsidy on Crop Yields

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
We use a Difference-in-Differences (DID) design.  
• Treated units (smallholders that receive the subsidy) are compared with never-treated units before and after the program starts (post = 1).  
• The coefficient on `treat_x_post` isolates the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT).  

Key identifying assumption: in the absence of the subsidy, the evolution of log-yields for treated and control farmers would have followed parallel trends. We partially test this with (a) unit and period fixed effects, (b) clustered standard errors, and (c) a placebo (“pre-trend”) check that pretends the policy started one period earlier.

## 2. R Code
```r
###############################
# Difference-in-Differences : #
###############################
# 1. Load packages (install if missing)
pkgs <- c("data.table", "fixest", "lmtest", "sandwich")
new  <- pkgs[!(pkgs %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
if(length(new)) install.packages(new, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(data.table); library(fixest); library(lmtest); library(sandwich)

# 2. Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s50_data.csv"
df   <- fread(path)

# 3. Simple DID (no fixed effects)
did_simple <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
coeftest(did_simple, vcov = vcovHC(did_simple, type = "HC1"))

# 4. Two-way fixed-effects DID with unit & time FE, clustered SEs
did_twfe <- feols(y ~ treated*post | unit_id + period,
                  data = df, cluster = "unit_id")
summary(did_twfe)

cat("\nATT (TWFE, cluster-robust) =", coef(did_twfe)["treated:post"], "\n")

#######################
# Basic robustness :  #
#######################

# (a) Add linear period trend interactions (unit-specific detrending)
did_trend <- feols(y ~ treated*post + i(period, ref = 1) |
                   unit_id, data = df, cluster = "unit_id")
summary(did_trend)

# (b) Placebo test: pretend the policy started one period earlier
df[, placebo_post := as.integer(period >= (min(period)+1))]  # shift by 1
df[, placebo_int := treated*placebo_post]
placebo <- feols(y ~ treated + placebo_post + placebo_int |
                 unit_id + period, data = df, cluster = "unit_id")
cat("\nPlacebo ATT =", coef(placebo)["placebo_int"], "\n")

# (c) Output neatly
results <- data.frame(
  Model      = c("Simple", "TWFE", "Trend FE", "Placebo"),
  ATT        = c(coef(did_simple)["treat_x_post"],
                 coef(did_twfe)["treated:post"],
                 coef(did_trend)["treated:post"],
                 coef(placebo)["placebo_int"])
)
print(round(results, 4))
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Agronomic evidence suggests fertilizer subsidies raise yields. Because `y` is in logs, we expect a positive ATT of roughly +0.20–0.30 (≈ 20-30 percent yield increase). Robustness checks should keep the sign positive; the placebo coefficient should be small and statistically insignificant, supporting the parallel-trends assumption.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log crop yields over time between treated and untreated units.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The subsidy program significantly increased crop yields.
